title: Your Post-Close Checklist: Insurance, Utilities & Handoff to Operations

slides.title: Hand off everything the closing team learned
slides.notes:
You own the house. This lesson makes it ready to become a rental.

You'll confirm the right insurance, move every utility and account into your control, and finish the safety work before anyone takes a photo. The main output is a dated operations handoff packet. It tells the launch team everything the closing team learned, including what's still open.

I'll follow Cedar Ridge the whole way. It's the course's hypothetical three-bedroom lake house with a dock, a private well, and septic, and it sleeps eight. Maya and Chris bought it with a DSCR loan, a rental loan the lender sizes mainly on the property's income.

Sam teaches the operations lessons, OP.1 to OP.5, right after this one.

slides.title: The two teams rarely talk, so write it down

left.head: Closing team
items: Agent, lender, inspector, title, attorney
Knows the dock railing is loose

right.head: Launch team
items: Insurer, cleaner, handyman, maybe a co-host
Hears only what you write down

box.text: Every open item gets an owner and a date.

slides.notes:
Up to now, your team was the closing team: agent, lender, inspector, title company, attorney. Now it's the launch team: insurer, cleaner, handyman, furnishing help, and maybe a co-host.

These two teams rarely talk. The inspector knows the dock railing is loose. The cleaner doesn't. The seller told you the septic company's name at the walkthrough. Your co-host will never hear it unless you write it down.

The handoff packet is how that knowledge crosses over. Every open item gets an owner and a date.

On your first property you're probably both teams. Write the packet anyway. The version of you answering a guest at 11 p.m. in February needs it.

slides.title: Read your policy as the operator, not the lender
items: Named insured matches how you took title
Short-term rental use covered, in writing
Liability limit covers the dock and water
Deductibles and exclusions
Loss of rental income terms
Insurer's conditions met, confirmed in writing
slides.notes:
You bound a policy before closing because the lender required it. The lender cared that the house was insured. You care whether a guest injury, a burst pipe, or a month without bookings is covered.

Pull the declarations page and the policy form. The named insured has to match how you took title in PA.10. The effective date should be the closing date or earlier. A standard homeowners policy may exclude business use, so get the insurer's answer on rental use in writing.

Check the liability limit for the dock and the water. Note the deductibles, read the exclusions, and check loss-of-rental-income terms.

For Cedar Ridge, the insurer required the dock railing and lower-level alarms within 30 days. Send proof and get written confirmation.

slides.title: Your own policy has to carry the full load
items: AirCover damage protection isn't insurance
Vrbo and direct stays aren't Airbnb stays
Most homeowners policies exclude flood
NFIP flood policies generally have a 30-day wait
slides.notes:
Now the platform. Airbnb's AirCover for Hosts includes host damage protection and host liability insurance. Airbnb says the damage protection isn't an insurance policy, not all damage is included, and AirCover isn't a substitute for your own insurance.

It also covers Airbnb stays. A guest who books on Vrbo or your direct site isn't an Airbnb stay. So your own policy carries the whole load, and AirCover is a backup that may help on some Airbnb claims.

Then flood. FEMA says most homeowners insurance doesn't cover flood. The national flood program generally has a 30-day waiting period, with some exceptions. If you skipped flood at closing, the clock may start the day you buy.

Get your insurer's answers in writing, including how the policy handles non-Airbnb bookings.

slides.title: Take control of every account in week one
items: Utilities in your name, on autopay
Well shutoff and UV lamp date noted
Internet speed tested in the bedrooms
A unique lock code per stay
No indoor cameras; disclose outdoor ones
Every login in a password manager
slides.notes:
Transfer every account into your name or your entity's name in the first week. Use the meter readings from the PA.11 walkthrough so the bills split cleanly.

Electric and propane go on autopay, with a propane delivery schedule. The well has no bill, but note the shutoff and when the UV lamp is due. Schedule the septic program, confirm trash pickup, and set up mail forwarding and plowing.

Test internet speed in the bedrooms. The smart lock gives each stay and each vendor its own code. Remove the seller's codes.

Airbnb doesn't allow cameras that monitor indoor spaces, even if they're off. Outdoor cameras and noise monitors must be disclosed.

Put every login in a password manager. Don't email or text credentials, and turn on two-factor sign-in.

slides.title: Build the vendor list while nothing is broken
items: Cleaner, $150 a turnover
On-call handyman, $150 monthly retainer
Septic, well, HVAC, and pest services
Night and weekend plumber and electrician
Plow service and trash hauler
A backup cleaner for a missed clean
slides.notes:
Your vendor list is the difference between a two-hour fix and a cancelled stay. Build it now, while you're calm.

The Cedar Ridge budget pays the cleaner $150 a turnover, the clean between one guest leaving and the next arriving. Set up an intro visit before OP.8 builds the cleaning checklist.

The budget also pays a $150 monthly retainer to an on-call handyman. Walk them through the whole house, including the dock, the septic, and the well equipment.

Most of the specialists came out of due diligence. Add an emergency plumber and electrician who answer nights and weekends, and one backup name for a missed clean. OP.7 covers the bigger co-host question.

Give each vendor their own lock code, and delete it when the job ends.

slides.title: File the permit and lodging tax on day 2

nodes.h: Add the number to the listing

slides.notes:
Diligence told you whether this address can run a rental. Now you file.

For Cedar Ridge, PA.9 found the seller's permit doesn't transfer. So Maya and Chris apply as new owners on day 2.

The same day, they register for lodging tax. That's separate from the permit, and it happens before the first stay. Lesson 3.3 in Part One shows how collection works on each booking channel.

Then you wait. If the local rules require the permit first, don't publish a listing before it's issued. Your local-rules checklist, SR.1, records the exact rule.

When the number comes back, Airbnb has a field for it. Bring the number and the exact holder name to Sam's OP.1. The licensing office and tax agency confirm the details for your address.

slides.title: Finish the safety work before any photos

left.head: Right after closing
items: Smoke and CO alarms working
Dock railing repaired
Clear exit from every bedroom
Clean well retest

right.head: During furnishing
items: At least one fire extinguisher
TVs and furniture anchored
Pool or spa drain covers

slides.notes:
Don't photograph a house you haven't finished fixing. Photos lock in what guests expect, and a listing can't promise a dock that isn't safe yet.

Start with the punch list from due diligence. Then walk the house against Airbnb's safety requirements. If smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are present, they must work and be tested. Blocked exits, exposed wiring, mold, and pests are on its hazard list.

For Cedar Ridge, the first group is the dock railing, the lower-level alarms, the well retest, and a clear exit from every bedroom.

The Consumer Product Safety Commission's rental tips add the second group: an extinguisher, anchored furniture, and drain covers. OP.6 builds those into furnishing.

Both groups finish before photos, on a one-page sign-off.

slides.title: $39,840.50 goes out before the first guest
slides.notes:
Maya and Chris closed on day 0 and plan to launch around day 45. That timing is an assumption.

The costs keep running with no revenue. PITIA on the DSCR loan is $2,557 a month. Add $450 for utilities, internet, and trash, $100 for software, and the $150 handyman retainer. That's $3,257 a month. Forty-five days is a month and a half, so $4,885.50.

The repairs from due diligence total $2,955: the dock railing, the alarms, and the HVAC service. Furnishing is budgeted at $32,000, and OP.6 covers how to spend it.

All in, $39,840.50 goes out between closing and the first guest.

The number to watch is the permit. Each extra month it takes costs another $3,257.

slides.title: After set-asides, only $2,379.50 is unallocated
slides.notes:
Maya and Chris had $231,000 of liquid savings at the offer. The $142,688 they put in already includes the furnishing. Take that out, plus the repairs and the carry, and $80,471.50 is left.

The set-asides come out of that. The property reserve is six months of PITIA, $15,342. The emergency fund is $51,000 from lesson 0.3. The weak-year reserve is $11,750, two years of the PA.9 weak case.

That leaves $2,379.50, under the $10,000 floor they promised to keep. They still save about $3,500 a month. About three months have passed since the offer, so roughly $10,500 puts them back above the floor.

The margin is thin, and it depends on that saving continuing.

slides.title: Every task in the 45-day plan has one owner
slides.notes:
Here's the shape of their plan. It's an assumption, but it's the shape I'd copy.

On day 0, Maya resets the lock codes, removes the seller's device accounts, and takes meter readings. In the first few days, Chris moves the utilities and Maya confirms the insurance terms.

On day 2, Chris files the permit application and registers for lodging tax. The handyman handles the railing, alarms, and HVAC between days 3 and 10. The well retest is day 12, and Maya runs furnishing from day 10 to 30.

The safety sign-off walk is day 30. Photos come on day 32. Chris builds the listing and publishes once the permit is done. Day 45 is the first guest.

Notice every row has one name.

slides.title: Put everything in one dated handoff packet
items: Property facts, floor plan, shutoffs
Insurance, flood, permit, and tax
Utilities, internet, access, and devices
Contacts and maintenance schedule
Safety sign-off and emergency plan
Every open issue, with owner and date
slides.notes:
Here's the exercise. Build the operations handoff packet and date it. Update the date every time you change it. If you haven't closed yet, fill it in for Cedar Ridge first, then copy the blank version for your own property.

The written lesson has the full template, 21 fields. Each row gets a source, a status of done or open, and the date you last confirmed it.

It covers the property itself, the coverage and permit, the accounts and access, the people and schedules, the safety sign-off, the reserves, and every row from your PA.11 unresolved items log.

Store it where your cleaner, handyman, and co-host can read it. Keep the credentials themselves in the password manager, not in the packet.

slides.title: Three rows must say done before you list

gates.q: Every open issue has one owner?

slides.notes:
The packet comes with three rules.

First, the listing doesn't go up until three rows say done. Insurance, with rental use and the conditions confirmed in writing. The permit, meaning issued, or the licensing office confirmed in writing that you may list first. And the safety sign-off.

Second, every open issue has one owner and one due date. 'We' is not an owner. If a row says we, it belongs to nobody.

Third, update the packet version whenever a vendor, a code, or a policy changes. A packet with the old cleaner's number sends your next call to the wrong person.

slides.title: Do these three things in your first week
items: Check your policy against the insurance list
File the permit and lodging tax registration
Start the dated handoff packet
slides.notes:
Three things this week.

First, pull your declarations page and check it against the insurance list. Write down anything you need to ask the insurer.

Second, file the short-term rental permit application and register for lodging tax. If you can't file yet, find out exactly what's missing. Every extra month costs Cedar Ridge $3,257.

Third, start the handoff packet. Date it, fill in the property facts, and write the names exactly as they appear on the deed, the insurance, and the permit. And reset every lock code if you haven't.

Next is Sam's OP.1. Bring your permit number, guest capacity, and safety disclosures. After Sam's OP.1 to OP.5, I pick up in OP.6 with the $32,000 furnishing budget.
